newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - WMX's Buntrock expects plan changes.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - WMX's Buntrock expects plan changes.

text.p: The sweeping restructuring plan adopted recently by WMX Technologies Inc will likely change when a new chief executive officer is hired, WMX Chairman Dean Buntrock said Friday.
In an interview with Reuters, Buntrock said: "We need a fresh look. He'll be expected to come up with his own plan and ideas."
Buntrock expects changes in the restructuring plan to be "inevitable."
In response to questions from investors at the annual shareholders meeting here, Buntrock said he plans to remain on the WMX board of directors for now.
"It's my intention to stay on the board as long as I can continue to make a contribution," he said.
Buntrock was elected at the meeting to a new, three-year term on the board. He said WMX is looking for a new CEO outside the waste industry.
"We've got the best people in the industry. We'd take someone out of the company if we were going to look at the industry," Buntrock said.
At the meeting, WMX board member Peer Pedersen said: "The (CEO) search is progressing very rapidly and very well."
Buntrock said the CEO search firm hired by WMX identified a number of individuals. He declined to provide specifics.

Also at the meeting, shareholders voted to change the name of the company to Waste Management Inc from WMX Technologies Inc. Four directors were elected to the board: Buntrock, Pedersen, Robert Miller and Paul Montrone. A proposed amendment for the annual election of directors failed, as did a shareholder resolution on director independence.

Major investors in the largest U.S. garbage hauling company asked numerous questions at the meeting. Most centered on Buntrock's personal plan, the company's commitment to the restructuring plan and the recent departure of former Chief Executive Phillip Rooney.
After the meeting, Lens Fund principal Robert Monks said he was encouraged by the meeting.
"There seems to be grounds for hope. They've picked good people to come in," Monks told Reuters.
At the same time, Monks said Lens Fund views Buntrock's departure from the WMX board as a likely necessary step.
"He's been such a major figure in this company that he's got to realize it's very difficult for a new man to have the sense of freedom he needs...I think (Buntrock) recognizes that," Monks said.
